title: Northern Kyushu in 5 Days — Fukuoka, Nagasaki, Dazaifu, Yanagawa, Mojikō
subtitle: Based in Fukuoka, with a day in Nagasaki, a day in Dazaifu and Yanagawa, and a day in Mojikō
summary: Five days in Fukuoka, setting out from Hakata each day: Dazaifu and Yanagawa, Nagasaki as a day trip, the retro quarter of Mojikō, plus Fukuoka city itself. Travel takes a large share of the Nagasaki day trip; that is the distance. Fukuoka Tower, Nagasaki's Spectacles Bridge and the Dazaifu Starbucks are held as alternates.

Kokura Castle closing days, Mojikō Retro Observation Room closing days, Mount Inasa ropeway fare.
Changes
This template takes only the Fukuoka and Northern Kyushu part of the travel log (days 1 to the first half of day 5); the Kumamoto and Aso part has its own template.

The travel log's first evening left the airport only at 21:00; this one arrives in the afternoon and adds Canal City Hakata and Nakasu yatai in the evening (originally the evening of the log's day 3).
The log's LaLaport Fukuoka (the Fukuoka Gundam) is not scheduled; for the alternates, check before you go whether that display is still there.
Travel log details
The stay follows the log: four nights in a row around Tenjin, Fukuoka; the log's author stayed at a hotel near Watanabe-dōri Station but found it dated, so only the area is written.
Entry and data
Register your immigration and customs declaration on Visit Japan Web before you leave: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
For data, use a physical SIM or an eSIM.
Getting around
Fukuoka's subway, buses, JR and Nishitetsu mostly take Suica and other nationwide transit IC cards; JR and Nishitetsu limited expresses may need a separate limited-express ticket or pass.

Airport to the city: the domestic terminal at Fukuoka Airport connects directly to the subway Airport Line, about 11 min to Tenjin and about 5 min to Hakata; from the international terminal take the free shuttle bus to the domestic terminal first (check fares and frequencies before you go).

Nishitetsu Dazaifu Yanagawa Pass: it can only start from Fukuoka (Tenjin) or Yakuin station and has two routes to choose from (Fukuoka → Yanagawa → Dazaifu → Fukuoka, or Fukuoka → Dazaifu → Yanagawa → Fukuoka); you cannot use the automatic gates and must use a staffed window; it is valid for two days including the first; you can only exit at Dazaifu and Nishitetsu Yanagawa along the way, and exiting at another station or returning early to the starting station voids the ticket.
The Yanagawa cruise takes about 60–70 min and the Shōgetsu boarding point accepts people until 15:00, so follow the order Fukuoka → Yanagawa → Dazaifu → Fukuoka and take the boat in the morning.

Nagasaki is a long day trip: the Limited Express Kamome connects to the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen, changing on the same platform at Takeo-Onsen; look up the last train both ways first, because the return to Hakata may run past 21:00.

The JR Kyushu Northern Kyushu Pass (the travel log's author bought the 5-day pass in 2023) does not cover the Shinkansen; Hakata to Kokura by Shinkansen costs extra, while the JR Limited Express Sonic or local trains are covered. This itinerary moves a lot; work out whether it pays for itself yourself.
Booking
The Nishitetsu Dazaifu Yanagawa Pass can be bought in person at Tenjin or Yakuin, or as a digital ticket online.
Book the Yanagawa cruise; in peak season and at weekends the wait can be long.
Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks game: check the fixtures first and only schedule the evening of day 4 if there is a home game; tickets can be bought on the day too, but the choice of seats is limited.
The Mount Inasa night view depends on sunset time, so the afternoon of day 2 can be shifted around it.
Other
Carry enough yen in cash: some shuttles, small shops and yatai do not take cards.
Nagasaki castella keeps about 12 days; umegae mochi must be eaten the same day.
Part of the permanent exhibition at the Nagasaki Atomic Bomb Museum is closed from Sep 2026 to Mar 2027; check before you go.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 5 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Fukuoka, with all five nights in the same area near Tenjin, so you never change hotels. Every day starts from Hakata or Tenjin: Nagasaki is a day trip, Dazaifu with Yanagawa is one day, and Mojiko with Kokura is another. The plan is to fan out from Fukuoka on the subway, Nishitetsu and JR.

Day 1: land at Fukuoka Airport in the afternoon, take the subway to Tenjin to drop your bags, wander {@d1-03} in the evening, have iron-pan gyoza for dinner, then go to {@d1-05} for the night view and street stalls.

Day 2: the limited express and the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen to Nagasaki, first {@d2-01} and Oura Church, lunch in Shinchi Chinatown, then the {@d2-04} and Peace Park in the afternoon, the night view from Mount Inasa, and back to Fukuoka.

Day 3: Nishitetsu from Tenjin, with the {@d3-01} in the morning, then on to Dazaifu after lunch for umegae mochi and {@d3-04}, back to the Tenjin Underground Mall in the evening, and Miyazaki beef for dinner.

Day 4: the Shinkansen to Kokura and then JR to {@d4-01}, up to the observation room, grilled curry for lunch, back to Kokura for {@d4-04} in the afternoon, and, if there happens to be a home game, the SoftBank Hawks at the dome in the evening.
Day 5: {@d5-02} and {@d5-03} in the morning, souvenirs at Hakata Station after lunch, bags back from the hotel, and the subway to the airport in the afternoon.
Where to sleep: four nights in a row in the Fukuoka Tenjin area, and on day 5 you check out and leave your bags.

Getting around: from the international terminal take the free shuttle bus to the domestic terminal and then the Kuko Line to Tenjin, about 11 minutes; Dazaifu and Yanagawa use the Nishitetsu Dazaifu-Yanagawa pass, which starts only from Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) or Yakuin, cannot go through the automatic gates, and is best done in the order Fukuoka, Yanagawa, Dazaifu, Fukuoka; Nagasaki is a long day trip on the Kamome limited express and the Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen, so travel takes a large share of the day, and you should check the last train both ways because you may be back in Hakata after 21:00; the JR Kitakyushu pass does not cover the Shinkansen, so Hakata to Kokura costs extra. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants one hotel and no moving bags, with daily trips out to Nagasaki, Dazaifu, Yanagawa and Mojiko. The Nagasaki day is tiring and the museum is heavy going, so leave some slack in your energy and your time.
